question: If AI agents remember everything between steps, who decides what they should forget?
reflection: Agents that keep useful notes could free people from repeating themselves, if we stay careful about what is stored and why.

sources.subject: Prime Intellect Agent, Meta Muse Code Terminal, Skills.sh v1.2 Upd

one_line: Coding agents that keep working in the background and remember their context are quickly becoming the normal way to build software.

top_stories.title: Open agent with lasting memory
top_stories.what: Prime Intellect released a free coding agent that keeps its working notes between steps and can rewrite its own instructions while it works.
top_stories.why: Agents that adjust themselves mid-task need clear logs so people can review what changed and why.

top_stories.title: Meta launches a terminal coding agent
top_stories.what: Meta released Muse Code, which runs several helper agents in parallel and can resume after a crash because it logs every action.
top_stories.why: Big platforms now compete on agents, so tool choices for small teams will keep shifting.

top_stories.title: Agent memory is getting expensive
top_stories.what: A new paper shows ways to cut the cost of what agents remember without losing accuracy.
top_stories.why: Memory cost will decide whether long-running agents are affordable for research teams.

saudi_lens.text: No direct Saudi link today, though agent memory raises the same data retention questions that national data protection rules already cover.

idea.title: Agent memory policy template
idea.pitch: A short template that tells teams what an AI agent may remember, for how long, and who can review it.
idea.first_step: Map one agent workflow and mark every point where it stores information.

idea_kids.title: The notebook robot
idea_kids.pitch: A role-play game where one child plays a robot who may only write three things in a notebook, and the group decides what is worth remembering.
idea_kids.first_step: Prepare small notebooks and a set of picture cards with things the robot sees.
